page: Vultr vx1-m-32c-256g-1920s is a memory-optimized server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz, featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled as a 1920 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong memory and single-threaded performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in large-block memory write bandwidth and single-threaded data compression, alongside strong performance in large-block read bandwidth and Passmark memory scores. Single-core CPU performance is strong, though multi-core scaling registers in the average tier. Cryptographic operations and database simulations, such as Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests, perform strongly, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high memory and local NVMe storage capacity relative to its compute footprint, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency compute cores. However, the 2.0 GHz base clock speed represents a tradeoff, as multi-core raw compute benchmarks remain average. This hardware profile is highly suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, text processing pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
